newsitem.title: USA: US to give N. Korea 85,000 tns corn, 10,000 rice. [CORRECTED 20:00 GMT]
newsitem.headline: US to give N. Korea 85,000 tns corn, 10,000 rice. [CORRECTED 20:00 GMT]

text.p: The U.S. will donate 85,000 tonnes of corn and 10,000 tonnes of rice to North Korea under two new food aid initiatives, a spokeswoman for the U.S. Agency for International Development said Monday.

In response to the latest appeal by the U.N.'s World Food Program, the U.S. will donate $27 million of grain -- including 30,000 tonnes of corn, 10,000 tonnes of rice and 5,000 tonnes of a corn/soy blend, the spokeswoman said. It would also include another 55,000 tonnes of corn.
The 55,000 tonnes of corn will move through World Food Program channels for distribution in North Korea by private voluntary organizations, the spokeswoman said.
The latest donation brings total U.S. food aid to North Korea over the past two years to $60.4 million.
(Corrects to make clear that 55,000 tonnes of corn is included in the $27 million new aid package).
The donated commodities will arrive in three or four shipments, beginning in late August. U.S. AID has already started the process of procuring the grain, the spokeswoman said.

Last week, a senior World Food Program official warned that North Korea could face mass starvation this year if its crop fails. A combination of floods in 1995 and 1996 and its own highly inefficient production system have left North Korea dependent on international food aid.
